The strongest upward pressure comes from potential Fidesz-TISZA coalition viability and polling momentum, while fragmentation and turnout uncertainty provide down/neutral counterweights.

question: Will any political party or coalition acquire a supermajority in the 2026 Hungarian parliamentary elections?
summary: Ensemble central estimate is high (72%), but objections suggest the path to a 2/3 majority is not guaranteed and may depend on coalition formation and seat translation rather than raw vote shares.
The strongest feasible path to a 2/3 majority is a post-election Fidesz–TISZA coalition capable of surpassing 133 seats, contingent on turnout and distribution rules in districts.
Polling divergence, turnout uncertainty, and the potential for third-party entrants to siphon votes introduce meaningful risk to translating votes into a 133+ seat majority.
While a constitutional 2/3 majority is possible, historical patterns and current volatility imply a prudent calibration below the ensemble point estimate.

justification.critique_assessment: Objections are valid and reveal genuine uncertainty around coalition viability, turnout effects, and seat translation, which materially temper the chance of a 2/3 majority relative to the ensemble's raw vote-share based signal.
justification.adjustment: Reduced from 0.72 to 0.60 to account for coalition-formation uncertainty, turnout variance, and translation of votes to seats; no downward adjustment based on implausible threshold breaches is applied.

forecasts.reference-class: Two-thirds majority (133+ seats) in the 199-seat Hungarian National Assembly, i.e., a constitutional-amendment threshold; anchored on post-1990 Hungarian elections and contemporary polling/seat-projection analyses.

sources.claim: 21 Research Center projections via PolitPro show Fidesz/KDNP at 96 seats and TISZA at 81 seats; the combined Fidesz+TISZA would constitute a majority (177 seats), indicating a plausible path to a two-thirds majority if such a coalition materializes.
133 seats are required for a two-thirds (constitutional) majority; across cited polls, no single party is projected to reach 133 seats, though coalitions could in principle surpass the threshold.
FT reports that the Tisza party was leading in major polls and discusses the possibility of a Tisza supermajority as part of a unified anti-Orbán effort.

Polls in Hungary show highly divergent results (Fidesz vs. Tisza leads); betting markets in the piece indicate varying expectations about who will win, highlighting uncertainty about achieving a two-thirds majority.
Polymarket-based odds cited in the Euronews piece show opposition-friendly bets with notable swings; bets imply unpredictability about the outcome and about a guaranteed two-thirds majority.
Polymarket odds show Magyar ahead (57%) and Orbán (39%); notes Polymarket as a market forecast; mentions that Fidesz previously won two-thirds majorities in 2010, 2014, 2018, and 2022.
Financial Times reports Tisza polling ahead of Fidesz and notes consolidation of opposition; discusses the prospect of a 'Tisza supermajority.'
Telex reports Tisza leading by about 12 percentage points among likely voters.
Reuters report: 21 Institute poll shows Tisza ahead (35% vs 28% for Fidesz) and Publicus showing 48% vs 40%; Our Homeland crossing threshold.
AP reports election date set for April 12, 2026, and notes emerging challenge from Tisza; polls indicate opposition gains.
IDEA Intézet poll (Feb 6, 2026): TISZA 48%, Fidesz 38%; seat share projection shows incumbents around 39.7% of seats.
Publicus poll (Feb 15, 2026): TISZA 48%, Fidesz 39%; other parties cross thresholds; discussion of seat distribution.
In 2010, Fidesz won a two-thirds majority in the 386-seat National Assembly.
In 2018, Fidesz-KDNP won a two-thirds majority (133 of 199 seats).
Election officials confirmed the two-thirds majority for Fidesz-KDNP in 2018.
IPU Parline confirms 2022 two-thirds majority (135 seats) in the 199-seat National Assembly.
Guardian reports 2018 two-thirds majority for Fidesz.
Reuters reports Tisza leading in pre-election polls ahead of the 2026 election.

causal-factors.name: Coalition path between Fidesz and TISZA to reach 133+ seats (two-thirds)
causal-factors.rationale: Forecasts projecting a combined Fidesz+TISZA tally around or above 177 seats indicate a robust route to a 2/3 majority if such a coalition materializes.

causal-factors.name: TISZA gains in polls relative to Fidesz
causal-factors.rationale: February 2026 polls show TISZA leading or challenging Fidesz in several surveys, increasing the odds of a non-Fidesz majority or a coalition that can exceed 133 seats.

causal-factors.name: Historical base rate for 2/3 majorities in Hungary
causal-factors.rationale: Two-thirds majorities have occurred in 2010, 2014, 2018, and 2022 under comparable rules, implying a non-trivial baseline probability when conditions resemble those elections.

causal-factors.name: Prediction markets indicating uncertainty about the 2/3 outcome
causal-factors.rationale: Market bets show divergent expectations and no clear consensus on a 2/3 majority, tempering the projection from the anchor.

causal-factors.name: Opposition fragmentation risk reducing seat consolidation
causal-factors.rationale: Even with anti-Fidesz sentiment, party fragmentation could dampen seat translation into a 2/3 majority due to distribution thresholds.

causal-factors.name: Turnout volatility with unknown turnout effects
causal-factors.rationale: Turnout swings could alter margins in various districts, but current data do not predict a directional tilt toward or away from a 2/3 outcome.

causal-factors.name: Coalition viability: Fidesz and TISZA forming a unified bloc to reach 2/3
causal-factors.rationale: A post-election Fidesz+TISZA coalition could plausibly reach well above 133 seats (e.g., 177 seats per PolitPro's projection when Fidesz/KDNP 96 and TISZA 81 are combined).

causal-factors.name: TISZA polling surge relative to Fidesz
causal-factors.rationale: Recent polls place TISZA ahead or closely competitive with Fidesz (IDEA Intézet February 6: 48% vs 38%; multiple polls cited in coverage), improving the odds that a coalition could cross the 133-seat threshold if votes translate into seats.

causal-factors.name: Opposition unity progress (parties quitting to back TISZA)
causal-factors.rationale: Financial Times reporting that opposition groups are consolidating behind TISZA to challenge Orbán suggests stronger anti-Orbán coalition potential and raises the probability of reaching 2/3.

causal-factors.name: Poll volatility/divergence and betting market uncertainty
causal-factors.rationale: Divergent polling results and mixed betting-market signals (e.g., Polymarket observations) create uncertainty about whether a 2/3 majority is achievable, tempering forecast confidence.

causal-factors.name: Third-party entrants crossing threshold affecting seat distribution
causal-factors.rationale: The presence and strength of other parties (e.g., Our Homeland near threshold) could siphon votes from major blocs and disrupt the seat totals needed for a 2/3 majority.

causal-factors.name: Historical frequency of constitutional 2/3 majorities in Hungary
causal-factors.rationale: Two-thirds majorities have not been routine since 1990; baseline frequency around less than half of elections implies a natural headwind to reliably achieving 133+ seats absent a durable coalition.

causal-factors.name: Opposition consolidation around TISZA as unified anti-Orbán front
causal-factors.rationale: FT reports that opposition groups are consolidating around TISZA (Péter Magyar), creating a plausible path to a 2/3 majority if the coalition wins enough seats.

causal-factors.name: TISZA polling lead across multiple surveys
causal-factors.rationale: IDEA Intézet (Feb 6, 2026) shows TISZA at 48% vs Fidesz 38%, indicating momentum that could translate into more seats if maintained.

causal-factors.name: Electoral-system bias favoring the largest bloc
causal-factors.rationale: Financial Times and related reporting note that Hungary's electoral rules can amplify the lead of the dominant bloc, aiding a unified anti-Orbán coalition in reaching 133+ seats.

causal-factors.name: Poll dispersion and uncertainty about coalition outcomes
causal-factors.rationale: Polls show highly divergent results and betting markets signal uncertainty about achieving a 2/3 majority, tempering confidence in a clear path to 133+ seats.

causal-factors.name: Potential for additional parties crossing the threshold to bolster anti-Orbán bloc
causal-factors.rationale: Polls indicate possible entry of parties like Our Homeland; a broader set of crossing parties could lift total seat counts toward or past 133 with a coalition.

synthesis: The objections identify a viable coalition route and key risk factors (turnout, distribution effects, poll volatility) that temper the ensemble’s 72% signal. Given these dynamics, a calibrated probability of about 60% better reflects the uncertainty around achieving 133+ seats, even if such a coalition could plausibly deliver it.
